text: Një nga ndërtesat më të larta të Nju Jorkut, Empire State Building i qendroi vendimit për të mos ndezur dritat bardhë e blu në me rastin e 100 vjetorit të lindjes së Nënë Terezës. Mbrëmë, ngjyrat e saj ishin e bardha, bluja dhe e kuqja, që simbolizonin një përvjetor tjetër, 90-vjetorin e amendamentit të 19 të kushtetutës amerikane i cili i dha grave të drejtën e votës. Qindra njerez u mblodhen mbreme ne proteste për t'u deklaruar pronarëve të ndërtesës se Empire State duhet të kishte nderuar para së gjithash Nënë Terezën. Nga viti 1931 e deri më 1972, për 40 vjet me radhë, Empire State ka qenë ndërtesa më e lartë e botës. Sot ajo është një simbol i fuqisë dhe i historisë së Nju Jorkut. Por qindra njerëzit që u grumbulluan aty dje pasdite besojnë se pronarët e ndërtesës hodhën një hap të gabuar duke refuzuar të nderojnë Nënë Terezën në 100 vjetorin e saj të lindjes. Protesta u organizua nga Lidhja Katolike por për shumicën e protestuesve feja nuk duket të ishte një temë me rëndësi. Shqiptarët iu bashkuan thirrjes së Ligës Katolike për të protestuar. Xho DioGuardi, i Lidhjes Civile Shqiptaro-Amerikane tha se dëshironte t'u kujtonte edhe një herë njerëzve se kush ishte Nënë Tereza. "Ajo është një idhull për botën, për katolikët ajo është qysh tani një shenjtore. Por ajo është një shenjtore patriote për të gjithë shqiptarët, pavarësisht nëse janë katolikë, myslimanë, ortodoksë apo edhe hebrej. Kam ardhur gjithashtu për t'u thënë pronarëve të kësaj ndërtese se ata bënë një gabim të madh duke mos e nderuar atë me ngjyrat e saj në 100 vjetorin e lindjes". Gjatë gjithë kësaj jave, cështja e ngjyrave që do të zgjidhte ndërtesa Empire State ka qenë në qendër të debateve këtu në Nju Jork, ndërkohë që disa pohojnë se nëse do të ishte gjallë Nënë Tereza nuk dë të kishte qenë dakord që për ditëlindjen e saj të bëhej kaq bujë. Mbrëmë, në një pjesë tjetër të Manhatanit, në katedralen e Shën Patrikut, shqiptarët e përkujtuan 100 vjetorin e Nënë Terezës me një meshë të madhe. Zgjedhja e kishës më të bukur të Nju Jorkut për këtë ngjarje i dha një solemnitet të pazakontë ceremonive. Mesha u dha nga Dom Pjetër Popaj, i cili drejton kishën Zoja e Shkodrës në Hartsdale të Nju Jorkut. Kleriku i bëri një përshkrim origjinës dhe jetës së Nënë Terezës, duke theksuar fjalët e saj: Me gjak jam shqiptare, me qytetari jam indiane ndërsa si besim jam murgeshë katolike. Në meshë kishin ardhur edhe njerëz të besimeve të tjera. “Ne kështu kem i qenë gjithmonë, kemi qenë një gjithmonë. Ne i respektojmë diferencat por e dashurojmë bashkimin me njëri-tjetrin,” tha Dom Pjetër Popaj për Zërin e Amerikës. Ai theksoi se shqiptarët janë sot një popull më i njohur në botë në sajë të lidhjes së gjakut që kanë me bamirësen e famshme.

text_en: One of New York's tallest buildings, the Empire State Building stuck to the decision not to turn on the blue and white lights on the occasion of the 100th anniversary of Mother Teresa's birth. Last night, its colors were white, blue and red, symbolizing another anniversary, the 90th anniversary of the 19th amendment to the U.S. Constitution which gave women the right to vote. Hundreds of people gathered in protest last night to declare to the owners of the building that the Empire State should have honored Mother Teresa first and foremost. From 1931 to 1972, for 40 years in a row, the Empire State has been the world's tallest building. Today she is a symbol of the power and history of New York. But the hundreds of people who gathered there yesterday afternoon believe the building's owners took the wrong step by refusing to honor Mother Teresa on her 100th birth anniversary. The protest was organized by the Catholic League, but for most protesters, religion does not seem to have been an important topic. Albanians joined the call of the Catholic League to protest. Joe DioGuardi, of the Albanian-American Civil League, said he wanted to remind people once again who Mother Teresa was. "She is an idol for the world, for Catholics she is already a saint. But she is a patriotic saint for all Albanians, regardless of whether they are Catholics, Muslims, Orthodox or even Jews. I have also come to tell the owners of this building that they made a big mistake by not honoring it with its colors on its 100th birthday." Throughout this week, the issue of the colors that the Empire State Building would choose has been at the center of debates here in New York, while some claim that if Mother Teresa were alive, she would not have agreed to her birthday being so uproared. Last night, in another part of Manhattan, at St. Patrick's Cathedral, Albanians commemorated the 100th anniversary of Mother Teresa with a large mass. The choice of New York's most beautiful church for this event gave an unusual solemnity to the ceremonies. The mass was given by Dom Pjetër Popaj, who leads Our Lady of Shkodra Church in Hartsdale, New York. The cleric gave a description of the origin and life of Mother Teresa, emphasizing her words: By blood I am Albanian, by citizenship I am Indian, while by faith I am a Catholic nun. People of other faiths had also come to the mass. "This is how we have always been, we have always been one. We respect our differences, but we love being united with each other," Dom Pjetër Popaj told VOA. He emphasized that Albanians are today a more well-known people in the world thanks to the blood connection they have with the famous charity.
summary_en: Large mass of Albanians in Manhattan to honor the world-famous charity

text_en: What are some of the details of the agreement of the European Investment Bank with the Municipality of Tirana? First of all, I thank you for this interview, as I believe that the signing of this project is very important for Albania. This loan of 80 million euros of investments, which was signed with Deputy Prime Minister Ahmetaj, is an important project to improve and develop the water supply network of Tirana. It is a clear example of how EU funds and the support of the European Investment Bank are going to the benefit of the citizens of Tirana. As a result of the project, about 1 million citizens will benefit from 24 hours of drinking water of excellent quality. I believe that this is a good example of how European funds and the EIB provide the necessary support. This is the largest EIB operation in Albania. I take this opportunity to appreciate and congratulate the Municipality of Tirana and UKT for the great work they have done, enabling us to achieve this important investment of 80 million euros. We also committed to provide a grant of 1 million euros in support of the implementation of the project and the preparation of the appropriate documents for the implementation of the project. What are the terms of the loan of 80 million euros for the improvement of the water supply network in Tirana? The project will be implemented in several stages. In the preparatory phase, initially the Tirana Water Supply and Sewerage Company and the Municipality of Tirana will prepare the feasibility study, for which they already have technical assistance and also with our help the tender documentation will be prepared, which will hopefully be ready next year. The tender will be announced and the constructors will be selected. We were informed by the municipality that the project will be divided into different lots, so that the work will be coordinated and done well, without burdening traffic and damaging the city's water supply. We will have to wait 4 years for this project to be completed. The COVID-19 crisis has hit the economy, and the European Investment Bank is coming to the aid of countries in the region to cope with the consequences. What is the focus of these investments in Albania? First of all I want to say that the EIB is part of the "European team" of donors and as part of the European financial institutions, we guarantee the setting in motion of mechanisms that provide rapid assistance to partners outside the EU, giving them support to overcome crises and recover. The EIB committed €1.7 billion to help overcome the pandemic crisis and its consequences in the Western Balkans. We are committed to accelerating the payments of existing projects as well as the swift approval of new investments in the Western Balkans. In the first 6 months of this year, we have signed investment projects worth more than 600 million euros in the Western Balkans, for this year alone. The signing of 80 million euros with UKT is the first project for this year in Albania, however, for the pandemic we signed an aid of 15 million euros through Procredit Albania, in support of medium and small companies, to cover their needs with liquidity. And now we are in talks with Prime Minister Rama and Deputy Prime Minister Ahmetaj, to decide which are the projects and sectors that we will prioritize, to encourage investments of strategic importance, by offering co-financing. As Prime Minister Edi Rama has said, there will be investments in infrastructure on the one hand and at the same time measures will be taken for digitalization, investments in environmental protection. Economic growth will also be strongly supported. As an investment bank, we will want to invest in interconnections, such as the railway infrastructure, the road network, the Tirana baypass and rural areas. We are discussing with the government about the implementation of these investments. We, as the European Investment Bank, in the event of the earthquake, offered 100 million euros for the recovery. The Prime Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Ahmetaj believe that our assistance should be used for the construction of affordable houses. This is a priority for the government and for us. And an additional grant for technical support assistance has been determined especially for groups in need. Albania has had to pursue a more prudent fiscal policy, due to the high public debt and restrictions dictated by the IMF. Is Albania an attractive market for private investment? The prudent fiscal policy as well as the prudent management of the public debt has been seen as a good trend of the government to overcome the difficulties brought by a limited budget, which must be properly managed and for the government's investments to be stable and at a good price. Recently we saw that the government came out on the market and sought to attract funding. As the European Investment Bank, we are ready to offer even more favorable conditions for the loans we offer. Compared to other financial institutions, we can offer long-term loans which go beyond 20 years with very, very favorable terms. These can help the government which can benefit from long-term loans at a low price, by investing in special sectors such as flood protection that is being discussed and worked on with the government. Also, as I said, investments will be made in the railway network, in digitalization, as well as in support of climate and environmental issues. How do you assess the measures of the Albanian government after the two disasters, the earthquake of November 26, 2019 and the pandemic, which is still ongoing? I must say that unfortunately no one in the world can make a projection of when the pandemic will end or the consequences of the pandemic. However, we hope that we will all overcome them and be able to return to the new normal. I must also say that just like everywhere in the world, in Europe, the economy declined. In the case of Albania, the decline was -3.5%. But we are already seeing that the recovery of the Albanian economy has begun, and it is happening in a sustainable way. There is a projection of economic growth at about 5% of the Gross Domestic Product. And this is encouraging for us and other European financial institutions which see the direction Albania has taken and the result of the measures taken was reasonable. The country has taken the path of recovery. Unfortunately, there are still many uncertainties related to the new variants of the virus, what impact it will have on the European and Balkan economies, and whether it will disrupt the supply chain because this is the main problem of the situation. Based on the uncertainties we are facing, we can say that the trend of stability and economic recovery remains positive, based on the increase in the number of vaccinations. Thus businesses will be able to reopen. If they were to see the analysis and observations recently made by our bank, focused on small and medium-sized enterprises, at the beginning of the pandemic most of these businesses, had to stop their work, beats 50-60%. The good news is that there is already a recovery and resumption of activities that are adapting to the new market reality, and digitalization is a very important element. However, there is a kind of caution in their plans and designs, but since there are no more provisions for a complete closure or suspension of activities, we can say that we are modest, optimistic. Because we are on the right line of recovery considering that we are still aware of the consequences and measures to be taken in the future.

Do të dëshiroja të përgëzoja qeverinë e Kosovës, veçanërisht organet e rendit, për punën e shkëlqyer që kanë bërë, që çoi në këto arrestime dhe përgatitjen e terrenit ligjor për vazhdimin e procesit. Kjo tregon se organet e rendit në Kosovë po e trajtojnë me seriozitet kërcënimin. Luftëtarët e huaj, nuk janë një kërcënim i veçantë vetëm për Kosovën. Shumë vende në Evropë dhe Shtetet e Bashkuara janë të shqetësuara për rrezikun që përbëjnë ata. Është e rëndësishme për ne që të bashkëpunojmë për ta përballuar atë. Përsa i përket ekstremizmit islamik në Kosovë, unë takohem shpesh me qytetarë të ndryshëm që ngrejnë shqetësime për të. Unë do të thoja që kjo është një çështje më problematike tani, se sa para dy vjetësh, kur unë mbërrita në Kosovë. Është një çështje që kërkon një shumëllojshmëri masash; bashkëpunim rajonal, bashkëpunim të organeve të rendit, por po ashtu edhe zhvillim social ekonomik, që të rinjtë të kenë mundësira, që të mos tërhiqen nga ideologjia radikale. Cilat mendoni se janë arësyet e radikalizimit të tyre? Në qoftë se situata në Kosovë po përmirësohet, çfarë i motivon ata drejt radikalizmit? Është vështirë të thuash. Di që ka patur arrestime të disa imamëve që dyshohet se kanë rekrutuar njerëz për të marrë pjesë në këto luftra të huaja. Ky është një faktor, por nga ana tjetër, ka njerëz që rekrutohen edhe në vendet e zhvilluara. Duhet një përpjekje e përgjithshme e qeverisë, e shoqërisë për ta përballuar këtë fenomen. Ky nuk është Islami i Kosovës. Kosova ka një traditë tolerance fetare me të cilën mund të krenohet. Dhe këtë duan shumica e banorëve të saj. Duke punuar së bashku, kam besim se ata do të ndikojnë që të mos përhapet radikalizmi islamik. Siç përmendët ju, duhet një përpjekje e bashkërenduar nga të gjithë, por a po bëhet kjo në Kosovë? Në disa raste po, por mendoj se kjo është pa dyshim diçka me të cilën duhet të merren qeveria dhe parlamenti i ri, përfshirë kalimin e ligjit për pjesëmarrje në luftra të huaja, që u miratua vetëm në leximin e parë në parlament, por pa u miratuar përfundimisht. Ky është një ligj i rëndësishëm. Mendoj se në të ardhmen, veçanërisht me arrestimet e fundit, apo pamjet makabre që kemi parë nga ISIS, pamje barbare dhe çnjerëzore, në Kosovë është krijuar një hapësirë e re për një debat më të madh mbi këto çështje.

text_en: The U.S. Ambassador to Kosovo, Tracey Jacobson, who is here in Washington these days, says in an interview with VOA, that the political impasse in Kosovo should be resolved by the political forces themselves and not with the help of other states. Focusing on Islamic radicalism, the American ambassador says that the authorities are treating this threat seriously and she calls for comprehensive efforts by the government and society to deal with this phenomenon. Regarding the Special Court, Ms. Jacobson adds that she cannot comment on an ongoing investigation, but emphasizes that Kosovo must go through this process in order to close this chapter of its history. My colleague Arben Xhixho spoke with Ambassador Jacobson. Madam Ambassador, three months have passed since the end of the elections in Kosovo and the governing institutions have not yet been established. What is your opinion regarding this political impasse in which Kosovo's politicians find themselves today? It is important to remember that this is the first time that Kosovo is holding general elections, since phase a of supervised independence ended. The elections were free and fair, the North participated in them for the first time and it is understandable that when a country goes through a new process, it takes longer. I respect Kosovo's institutions, I am pleased to see politicians in Kosovo addressing institutions, as was the case with the Constitutional Court. Now that the Court has given its verdict, I hope that political leaders will act swiftly to create the parliament, so that it can then move on to the formation of the government. It is not up to us to say how the process should continue, or how the posts will be divided, but we have common strategic interests with Kosovo, for which the parliament and the government are needed. Some of them are the continuation of the dialogue with Serbia, the establishment of the Special Court, the creation of the armed forces, the law on those fighting in foreign countries and a long list of tasks for the new government and parliament. In the past, the international community has helped establish Kosovo's institutions. There are many who think that even this time you can play an important role. As you said, this was the first election after the end of the independence watch, but not the first time that Kosovo has held free and fair elections. Do you think that you and your colleagues in Pristina will play any role in the formation of institutions? Are you willing to help by facilitating the process? I don't think it is the role of foreign embassies to facilitate what is an internal political process and that requires an internal political solution. What we do as the U.S. Embassy, or other embassies, is to urge Kosovo to adhere to the process under the country's laws and constitution to reach a democratic solution. It is important for Kosovo to do this without outside interference and this would be a signal that Kosovo is in fact an independent country, with a functioning democracy. What we have seen so far, with the referral of the situation to the Constitutional Court and the holding of free elections, I am confident that political leaders will be able to provide a solution to the situation. We will support them, we can advise them as friends but at the end of the day, this is their job as elected leaders. Do you think that new elections can serve as a solution, or are they not advisable? It's not up to me to say it. It is up to Kosovo's political leaders to decide. I hope to have a new parliament and government in the near future, due to the long list of issues I mentioned above. If it comes to new elections, the United States will be prepared to support the process, as it has done in the past, but I cannot rule out the possibility that in the coming days we will have a new parliament and government. As the new parliament is expected to complete work on the creation of the Special Court, Special Prosecutor Clint Williamson made public some general results from the investigations. What is your opinion, what is the position of the United States on them? The United States has supported the investigative group headed by Ambassador Williamson and will continue to support it in the future. We think it is very important for Kosovo to go through this process, this is the only way to close this chapter in its history. We were pleased that Kosovo's government and parliament made the right decisions supporting the establishment of the Court. It would be inappropriate for me to comment on the findings of an ongoing investigation. What is expected to happen now is the establishment of the Court and the possible prosecution of certain individuals. Defendants will have the opportunity, as in any other internationally recognized justice system, to be familiar with the charges, to answer them and to be part of a credible judicial process. Without being proven guilty by the court, they are innocent. We will continue to work with the Kosovo authorities, with the new parliament, to take the appropriate measures to establish the Court. There are critics who say that the Prosecutor's findings, published in that way, without name charges, have damaged Kosovo's image in general. Does this conclusion stand? Are you worried about this? I think political leaders in Kosovo, including the prime minister, reacted responsibly to the report. The Prime Minister reacted on the same day, expressing his commitment to support the process and I think that this is a sign of political prudence and on this basis we will continue further. Over the past few days, 40 individuals have been arrested in Kosovo on charges of links to the radical Islamic group ISIS fighting in Syria and Iraq. How worrying is that? Are we dealing with isolated cases, or is there greater radicalization in Kosovo? I would like to congratulate the Government of Kosovo, especially the law enforcement agencies, for the excellent work that they have done, which led to these arrests and the preparation of the legal ground for the continuation of the process. This shows that law enforcement agencies in Kosovo are taking the threat seriously. Foreign fighters are not a particular threat only to Kosovo. Many countries in Europe and the United States are concerned about the danger they pose. It is important for us to work together to deal with it. Regarding Islamic extremism in Kosovo, I often meet with different citizens who raise concerns about it. I would say that this is a more problematic issue now than it was two years ago, when I arrived in Kosovo. It is an issue that requires a variety of measures; regional cooperation, law enforcement cooperation, but also socio-economic development, so that young people have opportunities not to be attracted to radical ideology. What do you think are the reasons for their radicalization? If the situation in Kosovo is improving, what motivates them towards radicalism? It's hard to say. I know that there have been arrests of some imams who are suspected of recruiting people to participate in these foreign wars. This is a factor, but on the other hand, there are people who are also recruited in developed countries. A general effort by the government and society is needed to cope with this phenomenon. This is not the Islam of Kosovo. Kosovo has a tradition of religious tolerance that it can be proud of. And that's what most of its residents want. Working together, I am confident that they will influence the spread of Islamic radicalism. As you mentioned, a coordinated effort is needed by everyone, but is this being done in Kosovo? In some cases, yes, but I think this is definitely something that the new government and parliament need to deal with, including the passage of the law on participation in foreign wars, which was only passed at first reading in parliament, but without being finally adopted. This is an important law. I think that in the future, especially with the recent arrests, or the macabre images that we have seen from ISIS, barbaric and inhumane images, a new space has been created in Kosovo for a greater debate on these issues.
summary_en: U.S. Ambassador to Kosovo welcomes the work of the authorities in response to the threat posed by Islamic radicalism

text: Autoritetet janë ende duke punuar për të përcaktuar identitetin e atyre që sulmuan Kapitolin më 6 janar, shumë prej të cilëve me sa duket ishin të motivuar nga teoritë e rreme të konspiracionit se ish Presidenti Donald Trump fitoi zgjedhjet e vitit 2020 por se iu mohua fitorja për shkak të manipulimeve të gjera në zgjedhje. Teoritë e konspiracionit shpesh mbështeten në analizimin e prerë të gjërave në të drejta dhe të gabuara, dhe kjo mund t'i shtyjë njerëzit të bëjnë veprime që mund të mos i kishin menduar kurrë më parë, thotë Peter Ditto, një profesor i shkencave psikologjike në Universitetin Irvine të Kalifornisë. "Moralizimi i çështjeve i mobilizon njerëzit të veprojnë", thotë ai. "Nëse do të besoja se zgjedhjet amerikane ishin vjedhur nga fituesi legjitim, me siguri që do të sulmoja edhe Kapitolin. Është një veprim i llogjikshëm nëse kjo do të kishte ndodhur vërtet. Problemi është, se nuk ndodhi”. Sipas një studimi të Universitetit Emory botuar në revistën Journal of Personality, njerëzit që kanë më shumë gjasa të përqafojnë teoritë e konspiracionit janë më pak kërkues dhe shpesh shfaqin prirje narcisiste, të tilla si një ndjenjë e tepruar e vetë-rëndësisë, nevoja për vëmendje dhe admirim, marrëdhënie problematike, mungesë ndjeshmërie për të tjerët dhe që kanë një vetëvlerësim të brishtë. Nika Kabiri, eksperte në procesin e vendimmarrjes njerëzore pranë Universitetit të Uashingtonit në Siatëll, thotë se të gjithë tërhiqen potencialisht nga teoritë e komplotit, edhe pse disa shumë më tepër se të tjerët. “Ne të gjithëve na tërheqin potencialisht ato teori sepse të gjithë e urrejmë pasigurinë. Të gjithëve nuk na pëlqen ideja për të mos ditur pse ndodhin gjërat. Na bën të ndihemi sikur nuk kemi kontroll në botë. Ne duam shpjegim”, thotë ajo. "Është një tendencë e natyrshme që truri i njeriut të kërkojë shpjegime". Një teori konspirative është të fajësosh ose të shpjegosh një ngjarje të rëndësishme ose një grup rrethanash si një komplot sekret që zakonisht mendon se është organizuar nga njerëz të fuqishëm. Të menduarit në mënyrë konspirative gjithashtu mund të përqafojë idenë se nga publiku po mbahet një sekret i madh. Kur një personalitet i shquar, qoftë një regjisor filmi apo një president, përhap një teori konspirative, thotë ekspertja Kabiri, teoria e konspiracionit merr më shumë vëmendje. "Njerëzit i përkrahin këto besime sepse ata janë tashmë të pakënaqur", thotë ajo. “Ka diçka që duan, ndoshta, të shpjegojnë diçka që nuk u mbush mendjen dhe teoria u jep atyre një përgjigje për atë që e kanë parë si diçka të pabesueshme". Kohët e pasigurive, si pandemia, mund të ndihmojnë në nxitjen e përhapjes së teorive të konspiracionit. "Në veçanti njerëzit janë më të prirur ndaj mendimit konspirativ, janë të ndjeshëm ndaj këtyre teorive kur ndihen të kërcënuar dhe të shqetësuar, siç janë shumë njerëz tani," thotë zoti Ditto. “Kur bota duket konfuze dhe e pakuptueshme, si tani. Sipas ekspertit Ditto njerëzit shpesh përqafojnë teori konsiprative sepse nuk mund të pranojnë shpjegime të thjeshta për ngjarje tronditëse që u ndryshojnë jetën. Shumë amerikanë e kanë të vështirë të besojnë se Presidenti John F. Studiuesit e universitetit Emory zbuluan se njerëzit që kanë më shumë të ngjarë të përqafojnë teoritë konspirative janë shpesh më pak të pëlqyeshëm dhe më pak të ndërgjegjshëm, ndërsa shoqërohen nga ndjenja e së drejtës së patjetërsueshme, madhështia, depresioni dhe ankthi. text_en: Authorities are still working to determine the identity of those who attacked the Capitol on January 6, many of whom were apparently motivated by false conspiracy theories that former President Donald Trump won the 2020 election but was denied victory due to widespread election manipulation. Conspiracy theories often rely on the blunt analysis of things right and wrong, and this can lead people to take actions they may never have thought of before, says Peter Ditto, a professor of psychological sciences at the University of California, Irvine. "Moralizing issues mobilizes people to act," he says. "If I believed that the American election was stolen by the legitimate winner, I would surely attack the Capitol as well. It is a logical action if this would have really happened. The problem is, it didn't happen." According to an Emory University study published in the Journal of Personality, people who are more likely to embrace conspiracy theories are less demanding and often exhibit narcissistic tendencies, such as an excessive sense of self-importance, a need for attention and admiration, problematic relationships, a lack of empathy for others, and having a fragile self-esteem. Nika Kabiri, an expert in the human decision-making process at the University of Washington in Seattle, says that everyone is potentially attracted to conspiracy theories, although some much more than others. "We are all potentially attracted to those theories because we all hate uncertainty. We all don't like the idea of not knowing why things happen. It makes us feel like we have no control over the world. We want an explanation," she says. "It's a natural tendency for the human brain to look for explanations." A conspiracy theory is to blame or explain an important event or a set of circumstances as a secret conspiracy that you usually think was organized by powerful people. Thinking conspiratorially can also embrace the idea that a big secret is being kept by the public. When a prominent personality, whether a film director or a president, spreads a conspiracy theory, says expert Kabiri, the conspiracy theory gets more attention. "People support these beliefs because they are already unhappy," she says. "There's something they want, perhaps, to explain something that doesn't fill their minds, and the theory gives them an answer to what they've seen as something unbelievable." Times of uncertainty, like the pandemic, can help fuel the spread of conspiracy theories. "People in particular are more prone to conspiracy thinking, they are sensitive to these theories when they feel threatened and worried, as many people are now," says Mr. Ditto. "When the world seems confusing and incomprehensible, like now. When people are lonely and looking for connections with others." According to expert Ditto, people often embrace conceptual theories because they cannot accept simple explanations for shocking events that change their lives. A conspiracy theory about the September 11 terrorist attacks says that the twin towers in New York City fell from a controlled collapse rather than that planes crashed into them. Unsubstantiated speculation about the COVID-19 pandemic says that the virus came out of a Chinese lab and was probably a fabricated biological weapon. Many Americans find it hard to believe that President John F. Kennedy, an important political figure, was assassinated by a single gunman, an ordinary guy, so they embrace the unproven idea that there must have been a larger plot to assassinate the president. Emory University researchers found that people who are more likely to embrace conspiracy theories are often less likable and less conscious, while being accompanied by feelings of inalienable entitlement, grandeur, depression, and anxiety. "If you're in a close-knit community, whether it's on social media or in real life, with people who adhere to the same faith, there's a commitment to that belief that's even more intense than if you thought about it alone," Kabiri says. Ditto says that a million years of evolution pushes people to get into groups with like-minded people. "We are very tribal. We are really connected to people who are just like us. It's very unusual to have a place where you're supposed to befriend, connect and collaborate with people who don't look like you and don't have the same values," says Ditto. "The American experiment, in essence, is an attempt to work against all the forces of evolution and push people on this positive path where they collaborate. It's much easier to separate people."

text_en: In Tirana, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic and Macedonian Prime Minister Zoran Zaev held today the next meeting of the Open Balkans Initiative. They called on the other 3 Western Balkan countries, Kosovo, Montenegro and Bosnia and Herzegovina, to join this initiative. During the Meeting, 5 agreements were signed on the free movement of workers, on the identification of travelers at the border in integrated systems, and on food safety. The EU Commissioner for Enlargement, Oliver Varhejli, urged these three countries to continue this initiative. The night before, supporters of the former democratic president, Sali Berisha, held a protest rally against the "Open Balkans" initiative in front of the government headquarters, describing it as an initiative to the detriment of Albania and Kosovo and serves only Serbian dominance in the region. The European Union Commissioner for Enlargement, Oliver Varhejli, also participated in the next meeting of the Open Balkans Initiative with an online speech, praising this cooperation of the three politicians Rama, Vucic and Zaev and invited other countries in the region to be involved in their initiative. Commissioner Varhejli stressed that with their initiative they have understood the importance of regional integration and this initiative can accelerate the economic integration of the region with the EU. Commissioner Varhejli said that this initiative is an indication that the region is ready for integration and is doing so. "You can include me as a supporter for the Open Balkans. We think that any regional cooperation is welcome for the benefit of the Balkans and the EU. I invite the other 3 partners to join this initiative, which increases employment, economy and welfare and can change realities on the ground" - said Mr. Varhejli. Commissioner Varhejli said that the first intergovernmental conferences between the EU and Albania and North Macedonia have not yet taken place, but the time has come for this to happen and to bring all the agreements to the table. He added that only from this cooperation and through the concrete creation of the regional common market can the Gross Domestic Product for each country be increased by 1/3. Mr. Varhejli said that border facilities, recognition of diplomas and other documents are quite useful. "It doesn't make sense to connect to roads and trains and stop for a long time at every border. I urge you to continue and I hope that the other three partners will join you" - emphasized Commissioner Varhejli. At the opening of the meeting, Prime Minister Edi Rama reiterated the call for the other three countries to participate in this "fully inclusive initiative", because it injects dynamism into regional cooperation. "The Open Balkans is an aspiration more than an initiative. Every agreement here brings our countries closer to the EU, so other countries of the Western Balkans must join us" - said Mr. Rama. He said that today's agreements on the facilitation of exports, live animals, the free exchange of workers and goods are another step that will guarantee the 4 European freedoms. During the press conference, Mr. Rama said that today's agreements on the integrated electronic system of services, the free exchange of workers and goods, the facilitation of export and imports for live animals, are other steps that guarantee the 4 European freedoms and will be implemented as soon as the new year comes. "The Open Balkans is an implementing unit of the ideas and the Berlin Process and the common regional market, so I reiterate the call for the other three Western Balkan countries to join this initiative" - said Mr. Rama. President Aleksandar Vucic said that the agreements signed today are the result of extensive work of two and a half years. "The common goal is for the citizens of this region to live better in cooperation with each other, and everyone is welcome in this cooperation," he said. Mr. Vucic said that this initiative is much bigger than three politicians combined. "This is an initiative that will prepare the future of our children, to connect our citizens with each other, those who until yesterday have thought more about the past than about the future." He also emphasized that this is a comprehensive process and other countries are welcome. "If they want, they are welcome, but we don't have to apologize to them for not wanting to. They need to explain to their citizens why they are not here. When they see the benefits, they will come," said Mr. Vucic. Prime Minister Zoran Zaev said that visible steps have been taken together, and that the initiative is open to all countries in the region. "We have to show that we in the Western Balkans know how to work together and we know how to achieve successes together - he said. Kosovo refuses to be part of the Open Balkans Initiative since, as it is said, it cannot agree to be part of initiatives that may seem like a substitute for European integration processes. Kosovo's leaders said that they cannot become part of initiatives that do not fundamentally have the principle of equality, since Serbia refuses to recognize Kosovo's independence. Kosovo's Prime Minister Albin Kurti has on several occasions emphasized that the initiative is more like a Balkans that is open to influences from the East, separately from Russia and China and is not in line with Western values of democracy and the rule of law. The night before, former democratic mayor Sali Berisha and his supporters held a protest rally in the Albanian capital against the "Open Balkans" project and the visit to Tirana of Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic. Mr. Berisha and other speakers at the rally emphasized that this was not a protest against regional cooperation, but a protest against the Serbian project for Serbian dominance in the region at the expense of the peoples of the Western Balkans and against attempts to turn the Balkans into a zone of influence of Russia and Putin. The demonstration took place peacefully, with the exception of a few Serbian flags being burned by a few small groups of protesters.

text_en: In Albania, the hearing began today at the Court of Appeal for Serious Crimes, for the security measure against the former Minister of the Interior Saimir Tahiri, against whom two weeks ago, the Court of First Instance had confirmed the order of house arrest. The Prosecutor's Office has filed charges against Mr. Tahiri for "Trafficking in narcotics, in cooperation, in the form of a structured criminal group", and "Passive corruption of high state officials". Today's session comes after the complaint made by both Mr. Tahiri and the Prosecutor's Office. The former Minister of the Interior requests that his house arrest be lifted because, as his defense lawyer Maksim Haxhia said after the previous decision, "the former minister all this time has proven that he does not evade justice and that he himself voluntarily resigned from the mandate of the deputy". For its part, the Prosecutor's Office requests the arrest of Mr. Tahiri in prison. During the hearing in the Court of First Instance, prosecutors in the case stated that they have new evidence that testifies to Mr. Tahiri's ties to the Habilaj brothers and their group which was hit in Italy last October. Prosecutors said that they have facts that Tahiri was in the company of the Habilaj family and even that he intervened in the TIMS system, of the police that records entries and exits from the country, to erase the movements of Moisi Habilaj, one of the arrested in Italy. Last night, US Ambassador Donald Lu told the Balkanweb news portal that "we have heard several reports from independent sources about serious pressures in this case, including bribes that have been offered to judges". He called on "civil society and the media to observe this issue closely, so that the decision is based on evidence and the law and not on pressure, threats or money. No one is above the law", emphasized the American ambassador. Commenting on Mr. Lu's statement, Mr. Tahiri's lawyer said today that his message "was very important for the court to judge on evidence and law, and if that happens Tahiri should be lifted today the measure of house arrest." The investigations against the former Minister of the Interior began last October, under suspicion that he was related to the group of Habilaj brothers, his cousins, who were part of an Italian-Albanian organization which trafficked marijuana from Albania to Italy. The investigations were opened immediately after the Italian authorities cracked down on this organization in Catania, while in the wiretaps carried out, his name is mentioned several times in conversations between traffickers. The prosecution quickly requested the arrest of Mr. Tahiri, but the leftist majority rejected the request, claiming that it had not presented any evidence. At the beginning of May, Mr. Tahiri resigned as an MP by handing over the parliamentary mandate, while declaring that he wanted to be investigated and tried as an ordinary citizen without a political shield.

Kjo shifër është sa totali i viteve 2005, 2006, 2007 dhe 2008 të marra së bashku. Megjithatë, thotë zoti Stinson rritja është statistikisht e vogël. Dhe nuk është për mungesë përpjekjesh nga ana e prokurorëve, thotë ai. Në Shtetet e Bashkuara, ndjekja penale e një krimi të rëndë siç është vrasja pa qëllim ose vrasja e rëndë fillon me ngritjen e aktpadisë nga një juri e madhe. "Nga ajo që kam dëgjuar, të paktën në mënyrë rrëfimesh individuale, prokurorë nga i gjithë vendi më kanë shprehur vështirësitë që hasin për të bindur jurinë e madhe të ngrejë akuza,” tha zoti Stinson. "Ky standard favorizon policinë sepse u thotë anëtarëve të jurisë që ata duhet ta shikojnë çështjen përmes syve të një polici, jo duke e analizuar ngjarjen pas faktit të kryer dhe jo vetëm bazuar në përvojën e tyre, por përmes syve të një polici," thotë zoti Harris. text_en: Prosecutors in Minnesota took three days to file charges after the killing of an African American by a white police officer on April 11. Former Brooklyn Center police officer Kim Potter was charged last Wednesday with second-degree involuntary manslaughter in connection with the incident that left 20-year-old Daunte Wright dead during a traffic police stop, prosecutor Attorney Pete Orput announced. Former police chief Potter said the defendant had tried to use the shocker with electricity but mistakenly pulled out the revolver and fired. "We will act vigorously to prosecute this case and intend to prove that Police Officer Potter abandoned her responsibility to protect the public when she pulled out the gun instead of the shocker," prosecutor Imran Ali, a member of Prosecutor General Orput's team, said in a statement. Although the victim's family had called for the charge of intentional homicide to be filed, the fact that the prosecutor's office reacted within days by filing charges testifies to a qualitative change compared to a few years ago when investigators spent months before deciding whether to file charges against a police officer in similar incidents. "This doesn't happen usually anymore. People don't tolerate it anymore," says David Harris, a law professor at the University of Pittsburgh who focuses on law enforcement responses. The killing coincided with the final days of the trial of Derek Chauvin, the white former Minneapolis police officer charged with murder in the death of George Floyd, an African American, who died after Chauvin put his knee on his neck for more than nine minutes. The jury heard closing arguments in this case on Monday and has begun weighing the case. Ms. Potter, with a 26-year career with the Brooklyn Center Police Department, has pleaded not guilty. If found guilty, she could be sentenced to up to 10 years in prison. The fact that Ms. Potter was charged just three days after the tragic incident "is a big, big change," lecturer Harris said, although he added that "it's just not enough." The 2014 incident when a white police officer shot and killed 18-year-old Michael Brown Jr., an African American in Ferguson, Missouri, as well as the death of George Floyd, have helped spark a nationwide protest movement against police brutality. In response, prosecutors have reacted much faster to bring charges against white police officers for violating professional protocol, Mr. Harris noted. But in relation to the total incidents where the police use firearms against civilians in the country, the number of criminal charges remains too small. In 2020, U.S. police killed 1,127 people, making the United States stand out significantly compared to the rest of the Western world in terms of police firearm incidents, according to an analysis by the organization "Mapping Violence Police". Not a single police officer was found guilty of intentional or unintentional murder for years. In Minnesota, before Mr. Floyd's death, only one police officer had been found guilty of premeditated or intentional homicide after shooting an individual while on duty in 2017. Police work is often dangerous and even deadly, and law enforcement advocates say that a large majority of incidents with fatal consequences caused by the police end with the murder of an armed criminal. "Most fatal incidents where the police have a role are about the lawful use of force," says Cully Stimson, a former state and federal prosecutor and now deputy director of the Edwin Meese III Center for Legal and Judicial Studies at the conservative Heritage Foundation. The National Association of Police Organizations did not respond to VOA's repeated requests for an interview with the executive director. Public outrage over deadly incidents following the use of force by police is linked to the killings of unarmed suspects, often African Americans killed by white police officers. While whites make up just over half of the victims of incidents where police use force with fatal consequences, African Americans, who represent about 13% of the U.S. population, represent about 28% of individuals who were killed by police years ago, according to the organization "Mapping Police Violence". In recent years, protests against racial inequality related to police killings have led local and state prosecutors to file charges against a larger number of police officers involved in fatal incidents. Since the beginning of 2005, charges of intentional or unintentional murder have been filed against 140 police officers involved in firearm incidents that ended in fatal consequences. They led to the guilty verdict of 44 defendants, often on lighter charges, according to an analysis by Philip Stinson, a professor of criminal justice at Bowling Green State University. Only seven defendants have been found guilty of intentional homicide. Before the murder of 18-year-old Brown in Ferguson, an average of five police officers a year were charged with intentional homicide or involuntary manslaughter between 2005 and 2014, according to Mr. Stinson's analysis. But since 2015, the number has risen to about 13 per year. Moreover, since June 1 of last year, shortly after Mr. Floyd's death, 25 police officers were charged with intentional homicide or involuntary manslaughter, including former Atlanta police officer Garrett Rolfe in the murder of Rayshard Brooks, according to Mr. Stinson's calculations. This figure is as much as the total of the years 2005, 2006, 2007 and 2008 taken together. However, Mr. Stinson says the increase is statistically small. "Think about it, with all these cameras everywhere, we still have police officers charged in these incidents, which is really surprising to me," Mr. Stinson said. And it's not for lack of effort on the part of prosecutors, he says. In the United States, the prosecution of a serious crime such as unintentional homicide or aggravated murder begins with the filing of the indictment by a grand jury. To ensure the indictment is filed, prosecutors must first present the charges to a large secret jury, usually made up of up to 23 citizens. "From what I've heard, at least in the form of individual confessions, prosecutors from all over the country have expressed to me the difficulties they encounter in convincing the grand jury to bring indictments," Mr. Stinson said. There are several reasons why grand juries refuse to file indictments against police officers involved in fatal incidents, and why prosecutors do not try to bring charges in the first place, according to legal experts. A key factor is the United States Supreme Court's 1989 decision in a case known as Graham v. Connor. The judges ruled that allegations of excessive police force should be analysed from the perspective of a "reasonable and objective" policeman, according to legal experts. "This standard favors the police because it tells jury members that they should look at the case through the eyes of a police officer, not by analyzing the event after the fact was committed and not just based on their experience, but through the eyes of a police officer," says Mr. Harris. Unlike most other countries, the United States elects by vote, i.e. does not appoint local prosecutors, making them less enthusiastic about filing indictments in cases they know they cannot win. "They hesitate," Mr. Harris says. Another reason is that jury members, chosen by the general population, tend to have a generally positive opinion of police officers. In accordance with the Supreme Court's decision, they have been instructed to be guided by the concept that the policeman shoots in a dangerous situation, which evolves very quickly. "Juries are very reluctant when it comes to questioning the decision of the second that the police should make in situations that are likely to precipitate into violence," says Mr. Stinson. "In fact, we see the same reaction when the judges are the ones who make the decision in trials where there is no jury." But, although some juries continue to lean toward the police in situations that leave room for doubt, forensic expert Harris says there are signs that there has been a change over the past year. "I wouldn't be surprised if three years from now I would see more court verdicts finding the policeman guilty compared to the current percentage," he says.
summary_en: Justice experts explain that law and tradition make it difficult to bring charges, but add that the sensational murders of recent years are changing the situation.

text_en: Britain, France and Germany announced on Tuesday that Iran's steps in violation of the 2015 nuclear deal leave them no choice but to move the issue to a dispute settlement process set out in the deal's provisions. The countries say they have fulfilled their responsibilities under the Joint Plan of Action, including lifting economic sanctions against Iran and working to promote legitimate trade with Tehran. "However, Iran has meanwhile continued to break the key restrictions set out in the agreement," a joint statement said. "Iran's actions are contrary to the provisions of the nuclear deal and have increasingly severe and irreversible effects of the proliferation of nuclear weapons." The agreement, also signed by the United States, China and Russia, was intended to allay concerns that Iran was working to build a nuclear weapon and impose restrictions on its nuclear program aimed at making such a thing impossible. In return, Iran was relieved of sanctions that badly damaged its economy. But after the United States withdrew from the deal in 2018, Iran began reducing its compliance with steps such as exceeding the permissible limits of the amount of enriched uranium it can store, enriching it to higher levels and using more centrifuges than allowed. Iran did this through a series of steps, asserting each time that they were reversible if other signatories worked with Iran, mainly to help it economically after the United States imposed new sanctions. Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif said on Monday that the three European countries "had bowed to the American dictate" and that such an approach will never achieve anything. "E3 can save the deal but not by pleasing the bully and putting pressure on the responsible party," Mr. Zarif said on Twitter. "On the contrary, I must take the courage to fulfill my obligations." President Donald Trump's administration argued that the deal was too generous to Iran and did not curb what it called Iran's hostile behavior in the Middle East. It has carried out what it calls a "maximum pressure" campaign to force Iran's leaders to change their course. Britain, France and Germany reiterated their "regret and concern" at the US withdrawal from the agreement and clarified on Tuesday in their statement that seeking a resolution from the Joint Commission does not mean they are supporting the US strategy. "Our three countries are not joining a campaign to implement maximum pressure against Iran," the statement said. "Our hope is to return Iran to full compliance with its commitments under the agreement." The Joint Commission is made up of one member from each of the signatories, and according to the agreement they have 15 days to resolve a dispute. The step is the first in a series of possible settlement mechanisms, the latest of which involves referring the issue to the UN Security Council.

text_en: The next meeting of the Stabilization and Association Council between Kosovo and the European Union ended on Monday in Brussels, with the cancellation of a joint conference for journalists and a communiqué in which the European Union strongly criticized the tariffs imposed by Kosovo on Serbian goods and insisted on their immediate removal. Prior to today's meeting, Ms. Mogherini and two of her commissioners had asked Kosovo to remove tariffs and as a counterweight had offered to put Kosovo's name instead of that of the United Nations Mission in the Central European Free Trade Agreement, known as CEFTA. However, the Kosovo government has not accepted such an offer. Prime Minister Ramush Haradinaj said after the meeting that Kosovo aims for a comprehensive agreement with Serbia and does not have time for a partial solution to problems such as the issue of tariffs. He said that it should be resolved in an agreement that means recognition, a seat in the UN and membership in international mechanisms for Kosovo. He said that the Kosovo delegation has asked for equal treatment, emphasizing visa liberalization. While he reiterated the demand for talks on the normalization of relations with Serbia to continue, but with a greater role of the United States. "The government and I have never questioned the importance of dialogue. This is the only way forward for Kosovo and Serbia to become equal members of the European family," reads the speech that Prime Minister Haradinaj gave at the meeting and which he shared on the social network Facebook. "However, twenty years after the war, ten years after independence, and five years after the Brussels Agreement, the reality is that, progress towards normalization of relations between Kosovo and Serbia has been minimal, and in fact it has now gone completely off the rails, especially with the public discussion on the fatal idea of border correction and territory swapping; It has seriously damaged the credibility of the mediator, and has damaged the achievements we have made in the EU-mediated dialogue for more than 7 years." Anyone who talks about borders, territory, or any other correction to my decision, is our enemy," he said, among other things, in his speech. Kosovo signed the Stabilization and Association Agreement with the European Union in 2015, as a reward for its engagement in the negotiations for the normalization of relations with Serbia, which opposes Kosovo's independence, but opened accession talks due to its engagement in the talks. The European Union requires both sides to reach a binding, comprehensive agreement on normalization of relations before fulfilling the goal of becoming part of the bloc. But, the talks have already stalled and Serbia conditions their continuation with the removal of tariffs, which the Kosovo government imposed on November 21 as a sign of opposition to, as it was said, Belgrade's aggressive campaign against Kosovo's statehood. Kosovo's parliament on Saturday set up a negotiating team and adopted a resolution on the talks which rejects the possibility of discussing Kosovo's territorial integrity. The report underlines that the main risk in the country for money laundering comes from corruption, especially given the links in many cases of corrupt officials to organized crime that generate large sums of money and undermine the effective functioning of the justice system. Although the authorities are aware of the problem, law enforcement activity to crack down on these funds and efforts to clean them up has been very limited, the report said. Investigations, it is further stated, in a small percentage of cases lead to the filing of charges and this percentage is on the decline. But the statistics on confiscated assets do not seem to be consistent with the level of criminal activity in the country. The Council of Europe underlines that Albania is officially open for legal cooperation with other countries in cases of investigations under suspicion of corruption or money laundering, but adds that the legal mechanisms in operation are very complicated and involve multiple authorities with different timelines for requests and executions, concluding that these links hinder an efficient investigative process. In Albania at the time of the analysis, the report said, there was no system that prioritizes requests from other countries to investigate money laundering cases. The Council of Europe notes that despite the recent measures to expand the reporting of cases of money movements abroad by the Bank of Albania, the follow-up of activity suspected of money laundering or financing of terrorist organizations is very limited. The report notes that the Risk Level Analysis in Albania has identified an increase in the threat from religious radicalism and from recruitment efforts for terrorist activity. text_en: In Albania, despite the pandemic, the preparations of political parties for the April 25 general elections are increasing. Local activists, as well as Western experts and diplomats, today asked political parties to make their funding transparent in the April 25 parliamentary elections and to elect candidates as clean as possible without connection to the criminal world. The U.S. Ambassador to Albania, Yuri Kim, said that everyone wants the April 25 elections to be free and fair, this is the main goal, along with transparency on campaign and party financing, as well as the integrity of the candidates of a country that intends to enter the EU. Ambassador Kim made these comments at the conference on electoral integrity organized by the Coalition for Reform, Integration and Consolidated Institutions. "It is the responsibility of political party leaders to ensure that their candidates are clean, based on the strict standards of the law on decriminalization. After that, the people who really represent the Albanian people must be carefully chosen. Leaders should remove any politician linked to crime, and elect people who do not undermine democracy and do not promote corruption. Citizens should take responsibility not to receive money for their vote and not to vote for criminals" - said Ambassador Kim. While the chairman of the CEC, Ilirjan Celibashi, said that citizens are concerned that many deputies do not protect the interests of the community that votes for them, but follow the instructions of their financiers. "Just as money goes to politics, so will the next power; if the money goes regularly, the institutions will be transparent and accountable, if the money goes secretly and with corrupt purposes, so is the governance that comes out of it" - said Mr. Celibashi. At the conference, representatives of the ruling party also expressed their political will. The opposition expressed another of its concerns and doubts that the socialists are not committed to organizing elections with high democratic standards, changing the rules of the race, when the race has started. The conference discussed the possibilities of transparency of funding to parties, especially from private funding, which then bring clientelism in tenders, concessions and other public-private contracts. The orators urged the parties to move away from luxury campaigns, which are corrupted by merchants and private clients. There were even proposals that the financing of election campaigns entirely from the public budget, which can be more precisely supervised, not diverting the will of the people, but is a sufficient and transparent legal funding. As if the repeated irregularities in the electoral process such as family voting and vote buying were not enough, these elections will take place under special conditions dictated by the Covid 19 pandemic.

text_en: British officials authorized a COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use on Wednesday, giving the green light to the world's first vaccine against the virus and taking a big step towards ending the pandemic. The authorization for the vaccine, developed by U.S. drugmakers Pfizer and Germany's BioNTech, was granted at a time of rising coronavirus infections in the United States and Europe, putting pressure on hospitals in some countries and forcing new rounds of restrictions that have devastated economies. The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency, which licenses medicines in the UK, recommended that the vaccine could be used after reviewing the results of clinical trials showed that the vaccine was 95 per cent effective overall and that it offers significant protection for the elderly. British health secretary Matt Hancock told the BBC that the situation with the pandemic will improve in the spring. "Now we have a vaccine. The European Union criticized Britain's rapid approval of the Pfizer and BioNTech vaccine, saying the EU procedure is more complete. The measure to give emergency authorization to the Pfizer/BioNTech vaccine has been seen by many analysts as a political victory for UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson, who has led the country on exiting the European Union and has faced criticism for his handling of the pandemic. The decision was made through an incredibly fast approval process for urgent needs, which allowed the British drug regulator to temporarily authorise the vaccine, just 10 days after it began reviewing data from large-scale trials. In an unusual statement for open tones, the European Medicines Agency (EMA), which is responsible for approving COVID-19 vaccines for the EU, said its longer approval procedure is more appropriate as it is based on more evidence and requires more controls than the emergency procedure chosen by Britain. The agency said on Tuesday that it would decide by December 29 whether to temporarily authorize the vaccine from U.S. drugmaker Pfizer Inc and its German partner BioNTech SE. Other countries are not far behind. Regulators in the United States and the European Union are also verifying the Pfizer vaccine along with a similar vaccine developed by competitor Moderna Inc. British regulators are also looking into another vaccine developed by AstraZeneca and the University of Oxford. Pfizer CEO Albert Bourla called the UK's decision "a milestone".

text_en: Interview with Mr. Veton Surroi, founder of the Ora movement. Mr. Surroi, what platform is your movement coming out with in these elections? We have a platform for Kosovo's transformation within a period of no longer than 12 months, in which we will try to establish the rule of law, to start an investment cycle of 300 million euros, which will open up new jobs, for full management of economic flows in Kosovo. We have a platform of transforming Kosovo into a democratic state with an internal sovereignty. The issue of status will of course remain an open issue within a negotiated response with the international community. Mr. Surroi, you have often commented and made remarks on the way the problems in Kosovo have been dealt with. What do you intend to change? I think that a legal backbone should be established in Kosovo first; There must be the unification of all laws in a Kosovar legal system. Secondly, the competencies that are acquired rights of Kosovo, i.e. that are non-negotiable, such as the central bank, various ministries, including that of trade, etc., should be taken over. And third, politics needs to be reconstituted, so that it is put at the service of the citizens and not part of the negotiations between UNMIK and various political forces. Mr. Surroi, one of the main problems related to the elections is the participation of the Serb community. Belgrade, at least some of the politicians, called on Serb residents to participate in the votes, albeit on conditions, which the Albanian side immediately rejected. Albanian leaders have been criticized and are required to create a functional multi-ethnic society. Is Kosovo losing the battle to create such a society? And what does your movement offer for the improvement of the situation of the Serb residents, as one of the main standards? I think that Kosovar society has so far lost the battle in the political sphere to provide the necessary conditions for the majority, let alone the minority. And what is essential, is that the minority cannot be good, if the majority is not good. In Kosovo, the way the country is run must be completely and quickly changed. We need to make sure that this country is functional, and within a functional country of course we need to open a frank debate with minorities in order to ensure their inclusion. This form will neither provide Belgrade with the rights of Serbs nor allow the opening of dialogue between Kosovars, Albanians and Kosovars, Serbs. This will simply create an opportunity for Belgrade to be permanently involved in the process of consolidating and constituting Kosovo as a state. Mr. Surroi, you are a new movement, created only a few months ago, that will compete against some parties that have several years of experience. What are your goals for these elections, do you intend to get a majority, or to be represented in parliament, and why should residents vote for your movement? First, what we need to do is not repeat the mistakes that the parties have made so far, which have mostly dealt with empty debates over the past few years. We promise that we will go straight into issues that are fundamental to the functioning of this society, such as employment issues, the investment cycle, the radical transformation of agriculture, the stimulation of Kosovar experts, etc. We are talking about new jobs that emerge from this cycle of Kosovo's economic transformation. And this does not mean an illusory state, but a country which within 2006 should have its own constitution and not as has happened so far with these parties which have degraded Kosovo's constitutional and legal position through the constitutional framework and with a lack of reasonable vision of legal development,  Kosovo's economic and other economic developments. One last question, the Ora movement participates in the elections as a civic movement, and even you yourself are not called its chairman but the bearer of the electoral list. Can a civic movement be more capable than a political party of solving Kosovo's problems? But this is a political force in itself, despite the fact that it is not called a party. What we have so far is the experience of the debate, and citizens have increasingly begun to believe and understand what the essence of our message is. We have had a debate with farmers, with banks, with students, etc., and from these debates comes an efficient program of transformation of Kosovo into a state. With these programs and this support, which we are gathering day by day, I believe that we will be able to form an efficient government after the October 23 elections. You just said a little while ago that you will not leave the fate of Kosovo in the hands of the talks between Pristina and Belgrade, what is your position regarding the Pristina-Belgrade talks, when they should take place and whether they should take place or not? They must definitely take place, after the elections and with a consolidated government. In the talks, all issues that are of concern and that we think should be discussed should be opened. We, first of all, need to talk about all the damage that Serbia has caused in Kosovo, from the time of apartheid to the war period. Issues should be raised not as a technical framework, as has been done so far, but as real political issues that require solutions. Some of the issues are non-negotiable, such as the issue of Kosovar disappearances, which is neither a technical issue nor a matter of talks, but is simply a matter of regulating the timing and how to return all Kosovar missing persons to their homeland. The issue of war damages is an issue that needs to be raised, and also the issue of Kosovo's pension fund, which was stolen by the Milosevic regime.

Mr. Majko, if you will allow me, I would like to quote something from the speech that President Bush gave when he said that does such a concept exist in Albania? Does such a thing happen among Albanian politicians? I think so. Despite the fact that the public is used to looking, in the perception of the news that is offered in Albania, let's say facts, or the way of acting of politicians, which often make them sad, in general, Albanian politicians cannot be those of the years 1991-1992, where they shouted, cursed, did not speak verbally to each other, even when they came to delegations abroad,  They were separated and without talking to each other. There is a human communication and at the end of the day, what is called political prudence is knocking, I am talking about both the political class that belongs to the majority, and the one that belongs to the opposition. Now it is often about friends, about family friendships that left-wing and right-wing politicians have. Now we are no longer discussing only the alternative of this, or that, of this finance, or of that finance, but also the health of children, problems of various natures are also discussed. So Prayer Morning, as President Bush said, is a moment when we need to remember that in addition to being politicians, we are also people. Mr. Majko, Albania is one of the closest allies of the United States in the so-called "new Europe". How do you see Albania's role, your ambitions to join NATO, how much progress have you made so far? We see our relations with the United States of America and with the European Union as a very complementary moment. I am talking about the disagreements in the ranks of the Socialist Party. As you may know, yesterday former Prime Minister Meta sent a letter to the President, embassies, where he claims that he feels threatened by Prime Minister Nano. How do you see these developments and how much can the Albanian political system tolerate an ambiguity, or a lack of political stability? It is not that I am trying to throw a veil of optimism on what is happening in Albania. But I want to deal with what is full in the half-filled glass of water and not with what is empty. From this point of view, I think that of course among Albanian politicians there have been and will often be problems of a personal character, often clashes, insults and in the end the Albanian public is to some extent accustomed to such insults, or accusations, which often exceed the limits of normality. I am also talking about the parliamentary debates between the position and the opposition. But I believe that even you, as an Albanian from the United States, who follow Albanian politics, have seen very often that people who have accused each other of criminals, as in the case of Dr. Berisha and Mr. Nano, when it was the case for delicate moments of politics, have sat at the negotiating table, have found solutions,  They have found alternatives to stability. I have the impression that at the end of the day, after going through a series of problems, insults, insults, politicians have learned that money doesn't earn many points with the concept of insulting each other. text_en: The Patriarch of the Serbian Orthodox Church, Porfirij, announced today in Skopje that the Holy Synod of the Serbian Church has decided to recognize the autocephaly of the Macedonian Orthodox Church (COM) – Bishopric of Ohrid. Patriarch Porfirij made the announcement during a joint liturgy with the Macedonian Patriarch at the Church "St. Clement of Ohrid" in Skopje. Serbian Patriarch Porfirij said that the Assembly of the Serbian Church unanimously decided to respond positively to the prayer of the Macedonian Orthodox Church – Archdiocese of Ohrid for the blessing and recognition of its autocephaly. He announced that there will be a solemn announcement of the official act that will be organized together with the Macedonian clergy and then all Orthodox churches will be called upon to recognize the autocephaly of the Macedonian Orthodox Church – the Archdiocese of Ohrid. The news was welcomed with joy by the Orthodox faithful and the clergy of the Macedonian church. The decision of the Serbian church followed that of the Head of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Istanbul, Bartholomew two weeks ago for the admission of the Archdiocese of Ohrid to the community of canonical churches. The Macedonian Church broke away from the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1967 while the two republics were part of Yugoslavia, but the Serbian Church did not recognize independence and continued to treat the church of the smaller neighboring country under its own jurisdiction. Even other Orthodox churches did not recognize the autocephaly of the breakaway Macedonian church. The latter changed its name, i.e. added the attribute "Archbishopric of Ohrid" a few years ago to soften the attitudes of the Serbian church. The Macedonian heads of state welcomed the announcement of the recognition of autocephaly, as they congratulated the Orthodox clergy and believers. President Stevo Pendarovski emphasizes that the decision of the Serbian Church "will contribute to the correction of historical injustices and the spiritual uplift of the Archdiocese of Ohrid." Prime Minister Dimitar Kovacevski, who is in Italy, writes in a message that "the historic news represents the authentic part of the Macedonian identity". The decision to recognize autocephaly comes on a historic date marked by North Macedonia and Bulgaria. May 24 is known as the day of Saints Cyril and Methodius of Ohrid, who spread the Orthodox faith throughout the Slavic countries and as founders of the old Cyrillic alphabet. Until recently, the Serbian and Russian churches have insisted that the Macedonian church return under the autonomy of the Serbian church, while Bartholomew, according to those familiar with ecclesiastical circumstances, challenged this policy by ending the decades-long isolation of the Macedonian church. Analysts estimate that the new Serbian patriarch Porfirije intends to remove the Serbian church from the influence of the Russian church, demonstrating this by restraining from supporting the Russian aggression against Ukraine, even despite the popularity that Russia enjoys among the Serbian people. The heads of state in Skopje hope that the Patriarch of Istanbul, Bartholomew, will soon sign Tomos/decree on the autocephaly of the COM - Archdiocese of Ohrid.
